q: (Original MCQ #30) Who was the CM of KP before Governor's rule on 11 October 2026?
facts: Muhammad Sohail Afridi (PTI) became Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025, succeeding Ali Amin Gandapur. Governor's rule was imposed in KP on 11 October 2026.

q: (Original MCQ #50) Which country suffered atomic bombings in World War II?
facts: Two Japanese cities were hit by atomic bombs: Hiroshima & Nagasaki (August 1945). Japan formally surrendered on 2 September 1945.

q: (Original MCQ #66) In which year did Fatima Jinnah join the All-India Muslim League?
facts: She became active in the Bombay Provincial Muslim League from 1938.

q: (Original MCQ #67) Fatima Jinnah Joined the All-India Muslim League (Aiml) In: +?
facts: She became active in the Bombay Provincial Muslim League from 1938.

q: (Original MCQ #77) Bolan Pass Connect Quetta with?
facts: Bolan Pass connects Quetta with Sibi and the Indus plains (toward Jacobabad, Sindh).

q: (Original MCQ #86) Who was the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Kpk) before Governor's rule (October 2026)?
facts: Muhammad Sohail Afridi became KP Chief Minister in October 2025. Governor's rule was imposed in KP on 11 October 2026.

q: (Original MCQ #88) How Many Amendments are There in Constitution 1973?
opts: The Constitution of Pakistan was adopted on 9 August 1976, and had been amended 23 times as per source
The Constitution of Pakistan was adopted on 7 November 1972, and had been amended 23 times as per source
The Constitution of Pakistan was adopted on 12 April 1973, and has been amended 27 times (up to the 27th Amendment, November 2025)
The Constitution of Pakistan was adopted on 2 April 1974, and had been amended 23 times as per source
facts: The Constitution was adopted on 12 April 1973 (enforced 14 August 1973). As of November 2025 it has been amended up to the 27th Amendment (following the 26th in October 2024).

q: (Original MCQ #94) How Many Houses in Parliament?
facts: Parliament has two houses: Upper House called Senate (96 members), Lower House called National Assembly (336 members). Parliament is also known as Majlis-e-Shoora.

q: (Original MCQ #118) Largest District of Balochistan Area Wise is?
facts: Largest district of Balochistan (and Pakistan) by area: Chagai. Balochistan covers about 44% of Pakistan's total area.

q: (Original MCQ #127) Quaid E Azam presented his 14 Points in response to which report?
facts: Nehru Report was presented by Motilal Nehru (1928) and rejected separate electorates for Muslims. Jinnah's response, the 14 Points (1929), is called the "Parting of the Ways."

q: (Original MCQ #158) Radio Pakistan was established in which year?
facts: Radio Pakistan was established in 1947. Its headquarters is in Islamabad. Pakistan's first TV station: Lahore (1964).

q: (Original MCQ #162) First Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces?
facts: Last Commander-in-Chief (title before COAS): General Gul Hassan Khan. The title "Chief of Army Staff" was created in 1972, with Tikka Khan as the first. Current COAS (2026): Field Marshal Asim Munir.

q: (Original MCQ #182) Where is the Largest Salt Range in Pakistan Located?
facts: Salt Range's famous mine: Khewra Salt Mine (Jhelum District). Khewra is the world's 2nd largest salt mine. Salt Range stretches from Jhelum to the Indus River.

q: (Original MCQ #200) Safiyyah bint Huyayy's relation with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
facts: Safiyyah bint Huyayy was the daughter of a Jewish chief of Banu Nadir. She married the Prophet after the Battle of Khaybar and is among the "Mothers of the Believers."

q: (Original MCQ #204) Kashf Al-Mahjub Book Written by?
opts: Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh (full name Abul Hasan Ali Al-Hajweri)
facts: Kashf al-Mahjub is the earliest Persian treatise on Sufism, written by Ali Hujwiri. His shrine is in Lahore. "Data Ganj Bakhsh" means "Giver who bestows treasures."

q: (Original MCQ #205) Kashaf Al Mahjoob is Written by?
opts: Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh (full name Abul Hasan Ali Al-Hajweri)
facts: Full name: Abul Hasan Ali Al-Hajweri. Also known as "Data Sahib." His shrine in Lahore is visited annually during the Urs festival.

q: (Original MCQ #232) Which sword is associated with Hazrat Ali at the Battle of Uhud in the source?
facts: Zulfiqar means "Cleaver of the Spine." It was given during the Battle of Uhud and became a symbol of Ali's bravery.

q: (Original MCQ #247) Who became the first Pakistani woman to summit K2 in July 2022?
facts: Naila Kiani summited K2 on 22 July 2022, the first Pakistani woman to do so. Samina Baig was the first Pakistani woman on Everest (2013).

q: (Original MCQ #294) Relation of Hazrat Hamza with Hazrat Muhammad (Saw)?
facts: Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather, so he was the Prophet's paternal uncle. He was also his foster brother (shared a wet-nurse) and accepted Islam in the 6th year of Prophethood.

q: (Original MCQ #312) In which city was the first Islamic Summit held in 1969?
facts: OIC founded on 25 September 1969. First Islamic Summit held in Rabat, Morocco. Trigger for founding: the Al-Aqsa Mosque fire.

q: (Original MCQ #337) Abu Jahal Died in Which Battle?
facts: Battle of Badr took place in 2 A.H (624 AD). Abu Jahal was a chief opponent of Islam in Makkah, killed by Muadh ibn Amr and Muadh ibn Afra.

q: (Original MCQ #342) Liaquat Ali Khan made a famous 1950 state visit to which country?
facts: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 and addressed the US Congress.

q: (Original MCQ #346) Khenjar Lake Location Province?
facts: Khenjar (Kinjhar) Lake is also called Kalri Lake. It is located near Thatta district, Sindh, and is a major source of Karachi's water supply.

q: (Original MCQ #356) Who wrote the Punjabi Sufi romantic poem Heer Ranjha?
facts: Heer Ranjha is a Punjabi romantic poem written by Waris Shah (1766). Sohni Mahiwal, set near the Chenab River, is credited to Fazal Shah Sayyad.

q: (Original MCQ #372) Salt Range is in?
facts: Salt Range stretches from Jhelum to the Indus River (Jhelum, Chakwal, Khushab, Mianwali in Punjab). Khewra Salt Mine is the world's 2nd largest. Highest point: Sakesar (1,522 m).
